subject: Unstable TLS handshakes after private gateway cutover — database replication failing
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@hallcrest.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: Hallcrest Cloud Ops <infra@hallcrest.com>, Hallcrest NOC <noc@hallcrest.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Dec 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: [URGENT] replication TLS failures after private gateway switch

Vanessa / Redwood team,

Since we finished the private gateway cutover at 02:00 UTC we've seen repeated TLS handshake failures between our app tier and replica DBs. Symptoms: short-lived connections that fail during the TLS handshake (client Hello -> no Server Hello), and then a burst of retransmits. The apps show intermittent ECONNRESET and our DB replication stalls.

We collected a packet capture from the app subnet and traceroutes and attached them (hallcrest_capture_1202_08.pcap, traceroute-logs.txt). We're in production — impact is intermittent but frequent enough to affect nightly jobs.

Can Redwood ops help triage? Hypothesis from our side: the new on-prem edge appliance is doing fragmentation/MSS clamping inconsistently and there might be an asymmetric return path to your SNAT egress.

Samir
VP Infrastructure
Hallcrest Medical

Samir — thanks for the quick capture. I'm looping in Karthik (network eng) and Connor (private deploy owner) to triage immediately.

Immediate asks so we can prioritize:
- Karthik: can you confirm if our Dedicated egress SNAT ranges changed during the cutover window? If SNAT mapping moved between hosts we may be hitting session state loss when return traffic comes back to an alternate egress IP.
- Samir: can you confirm which on-prem edge appliance model (firmware) was deployed and whether MSS clamping/GSO was toggled? The capture shows multiple fragmented TCP segments but also some packets with ECN flags set — curious.

Vanessa

Subject: Re: [URGENT] replication TLS failures after private gateway switch

Thanks for the heads up and capture, Samir. Quick triage notes after an initial look at the pcap and traceroute logs:

1) Asymmetric return path + SNAT churn
   - The server-side SYN/ACK for some flows returns to an IP that differs from the original egress (multiple SYNs visible with different source path MTU markings). Our telemetry shows a failover event in the dedicated pool at 02:05 UTC — likely the same time. If return traffic hits a different gateway that doesn't have the SNAT state, the connection will be reset by the appliance.

2) MTU / MSS behavior
   - The pcap shows PMTUD blackhole characteristics: we see ICMP "fragmentation needed" for a subset of flows but the subsequent packets don't reduce their MSS consistently. There are also signs of GSO/GRO offload interacting with the appliance — some packets are large and fragmented mid-path.

3) Security groups & health check interference
   - Not directly visible in the pcap, but Hallcrest's healthcheck traffic from the newer gateway IP is being dropped by stateful devices on the DB side when expected ephemeral port ranges mismatch. This causes session pinning issues for long-lived replication streams.

Immediate mitigation suggestions (quick, non-invasive):
- Pin SNAT for Hallcrest's private subnet to a single egress IP for a 30-minute window so return path asymmetry is removed.
- Ask Hallcrest to temporarily lower MSS on the edge appliance (MSS clamp to 1350) while we verify PMTUD.
- Add an explicit security group rule to allow Hallcrest gateway healthcheck IPs to the DB replica port range (3306/5432) from the exact ephemeral range we expect.

I can push the SNAT pin and SG change if you approve (Vanessa). If Hallcrest can toggle MSS clamp we can validate before reverting. I also recommend capturing a short two-minute pcap with iptables TOS/DF clear to confirm whether PMTUD ICMPs are being blocked.

-Karthik
Network Engineering — Redwood Inference
